summary: Fog signal from 1883 on the Golden Gate's north shore; lens lantern lit 26 Nov 1900; keepers 1883 to 1960; grounds closed, seen from the bridge.

structures.note: One-story fog-signal building with the steam whistles; the light was mounted on its wall from 1900
Light tower on the wall of the fog-signal building (archive: tower established 1900)

access.note: The archive lists the station as not open to the public. The grounds are closed and the dirt road is not open to the public (LighthouseFriends). Visible from the Golden Gate Bridge and from bay cruises.

events.note: Fog signal (twin 12-inch steam whistles) placed in operation on 10 September 1883
One-story fog-signal building and keepers' dwelling built on the spur
Heavy storm and landslides carry away the trail to Sausalito; rebuilt on a new location
Lens lantern hung on the southeast corner of the fog-signal building's gallery, 19.5 ft above the water
Square brick light tower, its foundation mounted on the wall of the signal building
Boilers converted from coal to oil; cost of a day's operation fell from $25.44 to $6.91
Head Keeper John McKenna killed in a fall, 22 December 1902 (LighthouseFriends)
1906 San Francisco earthquake wrecks the large water tank; a 30,000-gallon redwood tank replaces it
Keeper Peter C. Nelson alerts the Fort Point life-saving crew to three young men in a disabled sailboat (LighthouseFriends)
Keeper Nelson again calls the Fort Point crew, for a man stuck on a cliff near Lime Point (LighthouseFriends)
Keeper Nelson falls into the bay while whitewashing the rock, 22 April 1913; rescued by his assistant, Ed Wiborg, and soldiers from Fort Baker
Point Diablo light and siren, 1.2 miles west, controlled from Lime Point; keepers take on the Point Diablo light
11 December 1932: fog signals run in a heavy snowfall; Lime Point among five stations reporting
Golden Gate Bridge completed; foghorn and light at its south tower make the Fort Point light unnecessary
Freighter India Bear rams the causeway to the station on 3 June 1960 while the fog signal sounds (LighthouseFriends)
Three-story dwelling and other outbuildings torn down

corrections.why: 1883 was the start of the fog signal (10 September 1883, LighthouseFriends). The lens lantern was first lit 26 November 1900 (Light-House Board report, fiscal year ended June 30, 1901).

corrections.proposed: fog_signal building, built 1883; square brick light tower on its wall, built 1900
corrections.why: The archive gives the light tower as square (Tower Shape: SQUARE) and established 1900, and the fog-signal building as constructed 1883. LighthouseFriends describes a one-story fog-signal building with the lantern added in 1900. No conical masonry tower of 1883 appears in either source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record and Wikidata give a conical masonry tower built 1883. The archive and LighthouseFriends describe a fog-signal building from 1883 and a square brick light tower added in 1900. The 1883 date is the fog signal; the light is 1900.
The 1883 date is the start of the fog signal (10 September 1883). The light first showed on 26 November 1900 (Light-House Board, fiscal year ended June 30, 1901).

notes_for_editor: 1) Current characteristic: the record gives Fl W 4s (from a NOAA ENC object) and focal height 4.6 m. Not checked against the Coast Guard Light List, which was not reachable; Wikipedia's infobox gives Fl W 5s for the current light, but it is not cited. 2) The Coast Guard Historian's Lime Point Light page could not be read: the live site returns 403 and the Internet Archive capture returns only the wrapper. It is not cited. Its search snippet gives 1900 as the first lighting. 3) The 1882 petition, the $12,000 appropriation and the 10 September 1883 start rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The Light-House Board report for fiscal 1883-84 is not in the local corpus (its Board reports run 1891-1901), and a Chronicling America search for 1883 California papers returned no hits. 4) The 1909 and 1910 rescues and the 1960 India Bear collision are LighthouseFriends accounts; no primary text was read. The 1902 McKenna death is LighthouseFriends, which cites the Sausalito News of 27 December 1902; not read directly. The 1913 fall is verified in The San Francisco Call. 5) Roster matched by name and position to the USLHS place 'Lime Point Fog Signal' (0.00 km). It covers the station's keepers as the archive lists them, with no separate roster for the light. 6) Differences: Joseph Pereira (LighthouseFriends 1902-1904, archive 1901-1904); Earl F. Mayeau (LighthouseFriends assistant 1953-1956; archive heads the line Principal). Both noted in the keeper notes. 7) Roster lines are as printed, with 'at least' spans kept. The 1959 armed robbery reported by LighthouseFriends is left out: it concerns a private person. Nieves Saldate and the Coast Guard names appear only as the archive prints them. 8) The LighthouseFriends statement that the station is being transferred to the Golden Gate National Recreation Area is undated; the story reports it as LighthouseFriends does. 9) OCR: the Bulletin and Light-House Board passages were read from their OCR text. The 1893 report prints 'aud' for 'and' and the 1901 report runs 'lenslantern' together; the story quotes the words as printed in full, correcting only those OCR errors, and the evidence entries keep the OCR text exactly. The 1901 scan p. 23 entry was read from OCR and the scan page was not viewed; cite it as scan page. 10) Atmosphere: every sensory or weather detail (the fog-signal hours of fiscal 1894 and 1900, the 1932 snowfall, the 1913 fall, the 1960 collision) is footnoted. No general period context was used. 11) Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story now states that the archive's place record lists no keepers' quarters while LighthouseFriends describes a two-story keepers' duplex. 12) Quotations from the Light-House Board (1893, 1894, 1901) and the Lighthouse Service Bulletin (1933) are quoted with the OCR's errors corrected in the story (for example 'aloug' for 'along'); the evidence entries keep the OCR text. 13) Not in the story: the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1918 (PDF p. 27) records Lime Point changed from a fixed white oil light to group flashing white with acetylene. The record has no characteristic_changed event for this; a human should check the current characteristic (Fl W 4s) against the 1918 change and the Light List.
